topics.topic: Validation, authorization, and unknown-field handling for MCP discovery requests
questions: Do discovery methods bypass operation/schema/actor validation entirely, or must each discovery request still fit a defined method schema after the three named checks?

After size, token and depth checks, do discovery methods answer immediately, or must they also pass a discovery-method schema and some authorization/actor check; and how are unknown fields in such requests handled?
After size, token and depth checks, must a discovery request also pass a method schema and the per-field bounds, or must it be answered immediately?

judgement.why: This is the same question about discovery-method schema, field and actor checks already decided by P1, and the relevant changed passage is the passage that precedent judged.

precedent.topic: Whether and when MCP discovery requests receive method-specific schema and unknown-field validation
quotes: answer_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST check one request in exactly this order, the first failure deciding: the byte length of request_bytes is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant, else invalid_request; authenticate_token with presented_token gives an Actor, else unauthorized with one fixed reason that reveals nothing about any record; the depth check of the request message below, else invalid_request; for tools/call, the message names a catalogue operation, fits that operation's request model as fit_request decides, called with that request model and the canonical_bytes of the arguments' JSON text, holds every bound below, measured on the fitted request before any JSON text in it is replaced, and has every JSON text it carries then made canonical by the replacement below, else invalid_request; the actor may call that operation by the actor table, else raise NotPermittedError; only then is the operation's handler called (A16 rule 1). initialize, ping and tools/list name no catalogue operation and are answered after the depth check, as the note on methods says.

answer_request: [BEHAVIOR] The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, parsed only after the depth check, which follows the size and token checks. A JSON object whose jsonrpc is "2.0" with a string method and an id is a request; one with a method and no id is a notification and one with no method a response: both are answered with empty bytes and change nothing. A request's method decides: initialize answers the result {protocolVersion: the imported MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION constant, capabilities: {tools: {listChanged: false}}, serverInfo: {name: the imported MCP_SERVER_NAME constant, version: the imported MCP_SERVER_VERSION constant}} whatever version its params ask, and keeps no state; ping answers an empty result object; tools/list answers {tools: [...]} as below, ignoring any cursor; tools/call names the catalogue operation in params.name and carries its request in params.arguments, which then pass the remaining checks of the first note.

answer_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] A refusal decided before the operation is known is a JSON-RPC error response whose error is {code, message: the refusal code, data: the RefusalAnswer as {code, reason}}: a body over the size ceiling is -32600 invalid_request; a token refusal -32600 unauthorized; a body nesting deeper than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant -32600 invalid_request; a body that is not JSON -32700 invalid_request; a body that is not one JSON object — a batch array included — or whose jsonrpc is not "2.0" -32600 invalid_request; a request whose method is none of initialize, ping, tools/list and tools/call -32601 invalid_request; a tools/call whose params is not an object with a string name and an object arguments, or whose name is no catalogue operation, -32602 invalid_request.
precedent.why: State 7 makes size, token, depth and JSON-RPC message validity apply, but reserves catalogue request-model fitting, field bounds and permission checks for `tools/call`; discovery parameters are not fitted and a `tools/list` cursor is ignored.

topics.topic: Availability or trapping of unlisted clock entry points
questions: Must those unlisted clock entry points work because A03's release-v1 trap list is exact, or be trapped because functions have no clock?

quotes:
The list is closed for the release; an
entry point found missing is added by a new release.
judgement.why: The closed release list leaves an omitted clock entry point untrapped until a new release, while A19 says functions have no clock.

witness.initial: A contract with an integer output has a non-empty trial corpus, and release v1 provides the standard-library function `time.clock_gettime_ns`.
events: An authoring agent submits an implementation whose `run` calls `time.clock_gettime_ns(time.CLOCK_REALTIME)` and returns the result.
The kernel runs admission over the corpus.
outcomes: Under A03's closed release list, the omitted entry point is not trapped and the execution can return a clock-derived value.
Under A19's no-clock rule, the clock access cannot be available to the function and the execution is refused as a sandbox violation.
witness.observer: The submitting agent observes different trial evidence and potentially a different admission verdict.
basis:
The runtime is one Python interpreter with its standard library and nothing
else, fixed by the kernel release (State 0 questions 4 and 17: photo processing
is the agent's own work outside the kernel), started with a fixed
hash seed (`PYTHONHASHSEED=0`) so that set and dict ordering repeats.

Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs
admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the
current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used.

Admission executes the implementation on every case of the corpus, in corpus
order, each as one TrialExecution M07, and never stops early — save for an
execution whose cleanup cannot be confirmed: it is recorded `crashed` with
`cleanup_failed` and the kernel stops (A03 rule 7), with no verdict
recorded; after the restart a submission runs admission afresh.

questions: May an authored trial case state expected values for only some output ports, and if so are the other outputs ignored or merely required to validate?

quotes: add_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise UnknownReferenceError for an unknown contract version; then RefusedError naming the first name in inputs that is not an input port of the contract version or repeats an earlier name in inputs, then the first name in expected_outputs that is not an output port or repeats an earlier name in expected_outputs, each taken by name in the order given; then checks each input port and, when expected_outputs is given, each output port, in port name order, by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for value ports and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIXTURE_BYTES_MAX constant for file ports, a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size and the port's media type; the first failing check, presence, carriage, schema then size, raises RefusedError naming port and check, and nothing is written. topics.topic: Sandboxed module import attributes and loader state
questions: Which ordinary import attributes and loader state must the module receive, including `__spec__`, `__loader__`, `__package__`, `__file__` and `__cached__`?

quotes: runner_source: [BEHAVIOR] The program MUST load the code file as a module named cabinet_sandbox_code with importlib.util.spec_from_file_location and module_from_spec, enter it in sys.modules under that name before exec_module runs its body and not remove it (A03 rule 3), and call the top-level run of the module object it loaded once with a dict holding one entry per input port, read from the files its configuration names: a value port has exactly one file, its JSON decoded to Python — for cardinality many that file holds the JSON array, which decodes to the list itself and is never wrapped in another —; a file port of cardinality one its one file's bytes; a file port of cardinality many a list of its files' bytes in order; it writes a crashed message, with the type and message of the exception when one escaped, when the module fails to load, has no run, or run raises. A MemoryError, or an OSError with errno EFBIG for a file past the file-size limit, that escaped run is written as a resource hit with that type and message, while ENOSPC or EDQUOT from exhausted host storage is an ordinary raised error; code that catches such an error and returns is judged by what it returned.
judgement.why: State 7 fixes an importlib-style loader using `spec_from_file_location`, `module_from_spec` and `exec_module`, which determines the ordinary module import attributes and loader state.

topics.topic: Time source used for HTTPS certificate validation
questions: Which time source decides whether an HTTPS certificate is currently valid: A19's clock module or the host/system clock used by the TLS implementation?

quotes: send_prepared_request: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] For https MUST verify the certificate chain against the host operating system's trust store and the hostname against the URL host, with the default TLS policy of the release's CPython (ssl.create_default_context()); no certificate, CA bundle or TLS option is configurable per service or instance, and a failed verification is a transport failure before anything is sent.
judgement.why: State 7 selects CPython's default TLS verifier rather than the replaceable kernel clock, so certificate validity follows that host-backed TLS implementation.
